graph.closure_explanation: Both original author packages are preserved. The Freya target closure includes its actual collector, iteration and free-parameter time results, the cited uniform PAGE specialization, its exact IID moment and descent proof, and numerical optimization dependencies. T13–T15 are classified by their numerical-comparison content; only required T15.case1 enters. Other PAGE sampling families, the PL theorem, unrelated Freya SGD, dynamic/lower-bound theory, experiments and T15 cases2–3 are not prerequisites of the requested tuned time guarantee. The user-approved independent-batch-timing strengthening is explicit and must remain in the plan deviation ledger. Source line363 supplies liveness; zero and infinite advertised bounds remain. Time uses a nonnegative extended integral, not a real integral that silently requires finite expectation. General-S T5 is a time-to-output prefix claim with proved output law transport; tuned T6–T7 retain literal final refresh via the sharper collector estimate. No graph approval or Lean proof is asserted by this candidate.

detail.construction:
Define Space d := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d); objective f x := (1/(m:ℝ))*∑i,f i x. RegularObjective enumerates differentiability of every component, global lower bound, Lminus gradient Lipschitz bound, Lplus mean-square bound, Lpm centered difference bound and supplied initial gap. It contains no algorithmic conclusions.
JobKind is single x or difference x y. Job holds component Fin m, kind, finite nonnegative start time and unique dispatch ID. Request holds current finite nonnegative clock and one pending job per worker Fin n. Query is Option Request; Reply is Option (worker, dispatch ID, finite nonnegative completion clock, vector). Define measurable structures explicitly by encoding these finite sums/products. Supply the canonical Option measurable-space instance by comap along None ↦ Sum.inl () and Some a ↦ Sum.inr a; use that same instance throughout the protocol. This shared supporting-definition/assumption module belongs in Proofs: the native role router permits assumptions in Proofs, while every Setups module must export a concrete spec. Only the five public specs belong in Setups. No Seed type restriction is added to Oracle.
jobWork is 1 or 2; jobValue is the corresponding exact component gradient or difference. deadline τ job i = start + jobWork*τ i in ℝ≥0∞. legalRequest means at least one pending job exists, every pending job starts no later than the current clock, and no pending deadline precedes it. Idle or empty-pending states use None, never a supposedly active empty request. PrimitiveService is joint measurability of answers plus a full oracle-tape measure set on which, for every call and legal active request, a real matching completion is returned: time is at least the request clock, at most every pending deadline, the chosen ID is the actual pending ID, and the returned value is jobValue. Idle queries return idle replies. This is primitive service behavior, not a batch time, variance or convergence bound. LiveService records finite actual next completion while a worker can finish; infinite advertised bounds do not create a completion at infinity. FreshAssignments describes conditional uniform selection from the current remaining multiset (full) or all components (difference); it will be proved from private seed laws, not required as an unexplained oracle guarantee.
equilibriumTime τ r := ⨅ j : Fin n, (r+(j.val+1:ℕ))/(∑i∈Finset.Iic j,(τ i)⁻¹), in ℝ≥0∞. largeSample m n := (n:ℝ)*Real.log n ≤ m.
Owned source contracts, including their scoped premises: FiniteSum: [average] f(x)=m^{-1} sum_{i=1}^m fi(x).
OptimizationAssumptions: [smooth_lower] For every x, lower<=f(x); ||grad f(x)-grad f(y)||<=Lminus||x-y||. [mean_square] For every x,y, m^{-1}sum_i||grad fi(x)-grad fi(y)||^2<=Lplus^2||x-y||^2. [centered] For every x,y, m^{-1}sum_i||grad fi(x)-grad fi(y)||^2-||grad f(x)-grad f(y)||^2<=Lpm^2||x-y||^2. [gap] f(x0)-lower<=Delta.
WorkerModel: [service] Each worker handles one assigned job at a time. Its completed value is the exact assigned component gradient; a difference job computes two assigned component gradients. Each primitive-gradient duration is nonnegative and at most that worker tau; simultaneous completions have a specified tie rule. [fresh_assignments] At every assignment, draw a fresh uniform label from the current uncollected multiset for a full collector, or from all m labels for a difference collector. Fresh Bernoulli refresh draws and the output-index draw are independent of the past and of these draws. [liveness] Some worker can complete its assigned computations in finite time, including after reassignment. Other workers may never finish. Every returned completion event is an actual finite-time event.
EquilibriumTime: [formula] t(r)=min_{j in {1,...,n}} (sum_{i=1}^j tau_i^{-1})^{-1}(r+j).
LargeSample: [large] m>=n*log(n).
edge_cases: d may be zero. m,n must be positive only in valid/source hypotheses. τ is sorted and may contain zero or infinity. Source liveness permits finite completions even when every advertised bound is infinity. Measurability and a common full-measure primitive-service event permit adaptive queries without uncountable null-set intersections.

ChoiceRow := (j : ℕ) → Fin (j+1), with the explicit countable product rowLaw of uniform Fin(j+1) laws. Use independent infinite arrays of such rows indexed by (batch,assignment), independent Bernoulli(ρ) refresh bits, and an independent uniform Fin(max 1 K) selector. Clamp ρ into Set.Icc 0 1 only to define invalid inputs; legality proofs remove the clamp on valid source parameters. All laws are explicit ProbabilityMeasure values.
chooseRemaining selects a uniform occurrence from an ordered finite set of remaining occurrence IDs using the fresh row coordinate cardinality-1, then returns that occurrence's component label. The row has this coordinate for every nonempty finite multiset, including arbitrary source Theorem12 multiplicities with initial cardinality greater than m. This preserves uniform multiset sampling; equal component labels remain distinct sampling occurrences. A full completion deletes one still-needed occurrence of the returned label, not necessarily the sampled occurrence ID. labelAt for difference jobs uses coordinate m-1 on valid m>0. No rejection sampling or unbounded number of RNG draws per assignment is introduced. Future rows, refresh bits and output index never appear in an oracle query.
Owned source contracts, including their scoped premises: PrivateSamplingLaw: [law] Use independent fresh rows containing a uniform finite choice for every possible remaining cardinality; independent Bernoulli refresh bits; and an independent uniform positive-horizon output selector. A row chooses a remaining occurrence uniformly, whose label is sent to the worker.
edge_cases: Seed laws remain defined for m=0 or K=0; invalid inputs halt before requesting a component. Positive-input proofs identify uniform Fin m and Fin K marginals.

detail.construction:
Implement complete finite-state transitions. FullState stores the original occurrence-label array, remaining occurrence IDs, sum, pending jobs, clock and next private-row slot. Dispatch all n workers initially from the remaining multiset. On a matching completion, delete one matching remaining occurrence and add value/initialCard only if still needed. Reassign the finishing worker uniformly from the remainder unless empty. DifferenceState stores S, x,y, count and sum; dispatch all n workers, add each of the first S completed differences/S, and perform the source final unused reassignment before returning. A dispatch is immediate; only actual completion replies consume the declared event unit. Both routines retain unique IDs. Batch initialization replaces obsolete pending work; prove the reset interpretation and do not wait for cancelled jobs. Invalid replies have a total fallback but admissibility excludes them on the full service event.
Owned source contracts, including their scoped premises: FullCollector: [full] Assign one fresh uniform remaining-multiset label to each worker. On completion, add the component gradient divided by |M| and delete one occurrence when still needed; discard obsolete completions. Reassign the finishing worker from the remaining multiset. Stop when all occurrences are collected.
DifferenceCollector: [difference] Assign uniform component labels at (x,y) to all workers. Sum the first S completed gradient differences divided by S, reassigning the finishing worker after each completion. Retain the literal final unused dispatch, but stop waiting after S completions.
edge_cases: Full multiset multiplicities must be preserved; do not change the source to a distinct-set collector. Empty remainder is guarded before drawing. Zero-duration simultaneous events are processed finitely; S positive in the source.

However, i) the big-$\mathcal{O}$ notation hides crucial dependencies on the smoothness constants associated with the functions, and ii) the rates and theory in these methods assume simplistic sampling mechanisms that do not offer any flexibility. In this work we remedy the situation. First, we generalize the \algname{PAGE} algorithm so that it can provably work with virtually any (unbiased) sampling mechanism. This is particularly useful in federated learning, as it allows us to construct and better understand the impact of various combinations of client and data sampling strategies. Second, our analysis is sharper as we make explicit use of certain novel inequalities  that capture the intricate interplay between the smoothness constants and the sampling procedure. Indeed, our analysis is better even for the simple sampling procedure analyzed in the \algname{PAGE} paper. However, this already improved bound can be further sharpened by a different sampling scheme which we propose. In summary, we provide the most general and most accurate analysis of optimal SGD in the smooth nonconvex regime. Finally, our theoretical findings are supposed with carefully designed experiments.

src_5625ccacde9e5ae0eb88ed58.quote: In practical distributed systems, workers are typically not homogeneous, and due to differences in hardware configurations and network conditions, can have highly varying processing times. We consider smooth nonconvex finite-sum (empirical risk minimization) problems in this setup and introduce a new parallel method, \algname{Freya PAGE}, designed to handle arbitrarily heterogeneous and asynchronous computations. By being robust to ``stragglers'' and adaptively ignoring slow computations, \algname{Freya PAGE} offers significantly improved \emph{time complexity} guarantees compared to all previous methods, including \algname{Asynchronous SGD}, \algname{Rennala SGD}, \algname{SPIDER}, and \algname{PAGE}, while requiring weaker assumptions. The algorithm relies on novel generic stochastic gradient collection strategies with theoretical guarantees that can be of interest on their own, and may be used in the design of future optimization methods. Furthermore, we establish a lower bound for smooth nonconvex finite-sum problems in the asynchronous setup, providing a fundamental time complexity limit. This lower bound is tight and demonstrates the optimality of \algname{Freya PAGE} in the large-scale regime, i.e., when $\sqrt{m} \geq n,$ where $n$ is \# of workers, and $m$ is \# of data samples.

At each iteration, the algorithm $A$ returns three outputs, based on the available information/gradients: time $t^{k+1},$ the index of a worker $i^{k+1},$ and a new point $x^k.$ Depending on the current time $t^{k+1}$ and the state of the worker, three options are possible (see~\eqref{eq:oracle_inside_random}). If $s_q = 0,$ then the worker is idle. It then starts calculations at the point $x^k,$ changes the state $s_q$ from $0$ to $1,$ stores the point $x^k$ in $s_x$ (at which a new stochastic gradient should be calculated), and returns a zero vector. If $s_q = 0$ and $t^{k+1} < s_t + \tau,$ then the worker is still calculating a stochastic gradient. It does not change the state and returns a zero vector because the computation has not finished yet. If $s_q = 0$ and $t^{k+1} \geq s_t + \tau,$ the worker can finally return a stochastic gradient at $s_x$ because sufficient time has passed since the worker was idle ($s_q = 0$). Note that with this oracle, the algorithm will never receive the first stochastic gradient before time $\tau$ (assuming that all oracles have the same processing time $\tau;$ in general, we will assume that the processing times are different).
